Class GtReceiptDefs

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.receipt.GtReceiptDefs
public final class GtReceiptDefs extends Object
Language dependent label definitions for the Grafioschtrader transaction receipt PDFs.

These labels are a wire format, not UI text. The generated receipt PDFs must be re-importable through the PDF transaction import. The import matches the text extracted from the PDF against the Grafioschtrader import templates in grafioschtrader-server/src/test/resources/testdata/import_template/*.tmpl. Those templates anchor the transaction values on exactly these label words. For this reason the labels are deliberately not placed in messages.properties: a harmless looking translation edit there would silently break the template matching. Any change to a label here requires the same change in the corresponding template files; the round-trip test TransactionReceiptRoundTripTest fails when generator and templates drift apart.

Constraints imposed by the template matching engine (TemplateConfigurationPDFasTXT):

  • Value lines are anchored on the first word of the line (SL anchor). Within one receipt every value line must therefore start with a distinct first word.
  • The transaction type word is captured as a single word and mapped via the template's transType= configuration, so type words must not contain spaces.
  • Numbers are always printed with Swiss separators (apostrophe grouping, dot decimal) and the templates declare overRuleSeparators=All<'|.>, making the import independent of the importing user's locale.

    • forLocale

      public static GtReceiptDefs.Labels forLocale(Locale locale)
      Returns the label set for the given locale. German gets the German receipt; every other language falls back to English, mirroring the two languages supported by the shipped import templates.

    • getTransactionTypeWord

      public static String getTransactionTypeWord(Transaction transaction, GtReceiptDefs.Labels labels)
      Returns the localized transaction type word printed in the receipt title and used in the PDF file name. For dividends on interest bearing instruments (bonds, money market) the word "Zins"/"Interest" is used; both words map to DIVIDEND in the import templates.
      Parameters:
      transaction - the transaction whose type word is requested
      labels - the language dependent label set
      Returns:
      single word identifying the transaction type on the receipt
